chunks: They have fear of God for His power over them, and act as commanded.
ai.seo_question: What does it mean that they fear their Lord from above them?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse is often interpreted as describing the angels, yet it also serves as a model for the righteous who maintain constant vigilance (taqwa) under God's watchful gaze. The phrase 'from above them' underscores the hierarchical nature of divine command, while their immediate execution of orders reflects the perfection of their will aligned with the Divine Will, a concept central to understanding the status of the Ahl al-Bayt and the Imams as the perfect executors of God's commands.
